title: Accelerating design-technology co-development using neural compact modeling and data-driven SPICE simulation
problem: Design-technology co-optimization requires rapid iteration between circuit designers and technology developers, but slow PDK (process design kit) release cycles and long SPICE simulation times create bottlenecks. Compact models are needed for fast, accurate feedback in technology development.
motivation: Accelerating design-technology co-development cycles is essential for scaling to advanced technology nodes, where model accuracy and simulation speed directly impact technology viability.
method: The approach uses machine-learning models that predict circuit behavior, combined with data-driven techniques that simulate design conditions without running the slow SPICE simulator. Pre-trained models quickly adapt to new manufacturing processes through fine-tuning. The data-driven techniques recreate design environments—accounting for instance binning, process variations, and layout-dependent effects—without actually running SPICE. This delivers fast feedback for rapid technology exploration.
key_novelty: Machine-learning models that efficiently adapt to new manufacturing processes, combined with data-driven simulation that replaces SPICE, accelerate design-technology iteration.
contributions: Neural compact modeling with efficient fine-tuning for process variants
Data-driven SPICE simulation using interpolation and derating
Elimination of SPICE runtime from design feedback loops
95% reduction in PDK release time with maintained model consistency and accuracy
primary_theme: Neural compact models for fast design-technology co-development
